author: lincoln_abraham
clause: Ask whether it is wise to attempt provisioning now, assuming it possible.
limit: No stated promise of bloodless passage, reinforcement, political reunion, or use of force. No unconditional offence follows from the question alone.

author: lincoln_abraham / course context
clause: Sustain the existing federal garrison in a retained United States fort.
limit: Read with Lincoln's maintenance instruction, not the calls-only by-kind rule of 0122. Union is the institutional purpose; success at political reunion is disputed.

author: seward_william_h
clause: Peaceful provisioning would warrant an attempt; expected armed passage instead initiates civil war.
limit: Offences depend on Seward's combat/escalation prediction. Not words in the President's bare question, not opening values, not physical impossibility.

author: chase_salmon_p
clause: Provision with reinforcement and a liberal but firm declaration; reject if armies and millions must immediately follow.
limit: Conciliation is the added declaration's term; caution is touched by a feared financial/war branch. Neither branch is assumed true for every adviser.

author: cameron_simon
clause: Do not spend lives and treasure on a temporary relief that cannot maintain authority.
limit: His answer relies on military reports; not an immutable cost or his starting caution cell. OR p198's 1875 endorsement is not the March document date.

author: welles_gideon
clause: The proposed tugs need armed fire to protect them, provoking hostilities and risking disaster.
limit: He disputes wisdom assuming possibility. On March29 he supports a differently qualified peaceable attempt with reinforcement if resisted.

author: smith_caleb_b
clause: Supplies alone are no lasting gain; sufficient relief and reinforcements would change the case.
limit: Preserves the unless clause and his distinction between holding this fort and enforcing national authority elsewhere.

author: blair_montgomery
clause: Hold property and enforce authority to reverse rebellion; firmness is expected to restore fraternity with minimal bloodshed.
limit: Fraternity is his predicted effect of firmness. He accepts the expedition's possible loss; this does not prove he lacks caution.

author: bates_edward
clause: Bare food supply prolongs privation without enabling revenue enforcement; armed passage risks general and social war.
limit: Right and physical power expressly conceded. His fear of servile war is retained as his racial/slavery context, not a narrator judgment or invented emancipation clause.

author: lincoln_abraham
clause: Ask time remaining, available means, additional means to supply and reinforce.
limit: March9 recounts the March5 submission. March12 question is quoted in Cameron. Do not invent a separately read March5 or March12 question original.

author: scott_winfield as quoted by cameron_simon
clause: Relief requires capture of all batteries and fleet, regulars, volunteers, organization and time.
limit: Resource and preparation requirements are not resources received by the runtime adviser. No feasibility score or quantity is injected.

author: joseph_g_totten
clause: A fleet needs land forces to capture and hold batteries; small tugs risk interception and repeated relief.
limit: Different tactical clauses from provisioning alone; Totten's reasoning is not an authored Lincoln escalation clause.

author: lincoln_abraham
clause: Prepare sea expedition with ships, troops and stores, in cooperation between War and Navy.
limit: Preparation is not sailing, attack, receipt, success, or authority to execute every adviser's proposed alternative.

author: welles_gideon;chase_salmon_p
clause: Announce a peaceable provisioning attempt; armed resistance warrants reinforcement.
limit: Retain the no-molestation/armed-resistance distinction and independent defense of Pickens. No automatic transition on date.

author: seward_william_h
clause: Preparation itself becomes known and provokes a war at an untenable Charleston position.
limit: Against this expedition while willing to prepare for defensive war at Pensacola/Texas. Not against all federal defense.

author: seward_william_h;smith_caleb_b;bates_edward
clause: Withdraw Sumter to avoid an unnecessary collision, while retaining other federal defenses and legal authority.
limit: Union/order are the expressly retained wider purpose and concurrent measures, not a guarantee that withdrawal achieves reunion.

author: smith_caleb_b
clause: If understood as surrendering enforcement and allowing rebellion its course, withdrawal is disastrous.
limit: The if clause is indispensable; the same paper denies that meaning when other forts and authority are defended.

author: blair_montgomery
clause: Leaving an acknowledged relievable Sumter emboldens rebellion and endangers federal authority and reunion.
limit: Expected bloody strife is his prediction; no unconditional union/duty offence is proved merely by the word evacuation.

author: scott_winfield
clause: Sumter will have to be abandoned sooner or later; early voluntary withdrawal is more graceful.
limit: Military necessity is Scott's assessment, not a universal course term. This Sumter-only withdrawal is not his two-fort proposal.

author: scott_winfield
clause: Evacuate Sumter AND Pickens as an act of liberality to retain the eight wavering slaveholding states and recover the two states.
limit: Scott explicitly proposes reunion, not Confederate independence. The printed memorandum is undated. No exact authored or receipt date inferred from the 15-March enclosure grouping.

author: scott_winfield
clause: Jefferson and Taylor depend on different principles and should never be abandoned.
limit: Retained defenses are part of his programme. Not an instruction to evacuate every southern fort.

author: lincoln_abraham / contrast with Scott proposal
clause: Giving up held positions limits the earlier instruction to maintain all retained military places.
limit: [I] A bounded conflict with the maintenance instruction, not proof of disloyalty or an adviser's refusal to do duty. Authority to adopt/execute a programme is outside S131.

author: seward_william_h
clause: Discuss whether conciliation demoralizes the Republican party and whether preserving country warrants sacrificing party.
limit: A debated party consequence, not a term of Lincoln's question. No unconditional party offence or party-based answer table recommended.

author: anderson_robert quoted by cameron_simon; cabinet respondents
clause: Personal risk to Anderson's reputation; national honor, credibility and public reaction discussed by others.
limit: Anderson's own reputation is not Cameron's motive. Government prestige and sailors' honor are not a cabinet member's personal reputation cell. No generic reputation offence recommended.
